# Main

## Isabel Fernández Escapa {#title}

### MICROBIOLOGY \| BIOINFORMATICS \| INFRASTRUCTURE 

Computational microbiologist with 15+ years of experience building reproducible workflows that accelerate discovery and make complex data accessible to interdisciplinary teams. I combine deep knowledge of bacterial physiology and microbial communities with a proven ability to design and deploy scalable bioinformatics systems. A proficient problem solver who bridges wet-lab science and computational engineering, capable of envisioning product solutions and driving them from concept to deployment while working closely with laboratory scientists, product managers, software developers, and senior leadership.


## Professional Experience {data-icon="briefcase"}

### Assistant Professor (K.P. Lemon Lab)

Baylor College of Medicine, MVM Dept.

Houston, TX

Jul/2024 - Present

-   Built an interactive Shiny app providing customizable access to complex RNASeq datasets empowering researchers without computational expertise to explore results independently.
-   Designed a Data Analysis and Laboratory Information Integrity Core for a multi-PI grant proposal, encompassing standardized pipelines for multi-omics, FAIR data management frameworks, and visualization dashboards across collaborative projects.
-   Contributed to all lab grant proposals as bioinformatics lead, providing preliminary analyses, visualizations, and methodological sections, as well as input on experimental design and overall scientific scope.

### Bioinformatics Manager (K.P. Lemon Lab)

Baylor College of Medicine, MVM Dept.

Houston, TX

May/2023 - Jun/2024

-   Architected a data management framework integrating code version control and data storage, with portable environment variable configurations enabling reproducible code execution across team members' systems.
-   Established bioinformatics workflows, including pangenomics, phylogenomics, metabolic predictions, and host-microbe dual RNASeq.
-   Mentored and supervised technicians and students in programming, data visualization, statistical modeling, and best documentation practices to ensure scientific rigor and reproducibility across all lab publications.


### Associate Director, Bioinformatics

Pandemic Response Lab (PRL)

New York City, NY

Jun/2022 - Feb/2023

-   Provided subject matter expertise on the streamlining and automation of end to end NGS lab operations: sample accessioning, LIMS design, bioinformatic and QC analysis, report generation and data delivery.
-   Designed the architecture and supervised the development of a NextFlow based modular environment to fully automate all bioinformatic steps, including integration with in-house LIMS system, QC analysis, and data storage/delivery.
-   Supervised implementation of a QC bioinformatics pipeline to assist R&D efforts on the development of a hybrid capture oncological panel.
-   Supervised team operations for multiple workflows delivering data to customers within a tight schedule, including COVID-19 surveillance from both clinical and wastewater samples, RNA-seq, hybrid capture, whole-genome and plasmid sequencing.

### Principal Scientist, Bioinformatics

Pandemic Response Lab (PRL)

New York City, NY

Jul/2021 - Jun/2022

-   Single handedly designed, built and maintained a dashboard for NGS QC report generation to assist operations on a high throughput sequencing production laboratory.
-   Built and managed a team, provided training to perform routine analytical tasks, as well as mentorship and supervision to develop independent work.


### Senior Bioinformatics Scientist

Pandemic Response Lab (PRL)

New York City, NY

Apr/2021 - Jul/2021

-   Participated on developing and optimizing a SARS-CoV-2 amplicon sequencing bioinformatics workflow for NGS Illumina data.
-   Established a workflow for weekly submission of SARS-CoV-2 sequencing data to public repositories (GISAID and NCBI/SRA).

### Senior Staff Scientist, Bioinformatics

Baylor College of Medicine, MVM Dept.

Houston, TX

Sep/2019 - Apr/2021

-   Established a workflow for exploring genomic diversity using Pangenomics & Phylogenomics (using PanACoTa, Anvio, PPanGGOLiN, GET_HOMOLOGUES, and GET_PHYLOMARKERS).
-   Assisted in the design of bioinformatic pipelines to analyze data derived from microbe-microbe and host-microbe interactions in Human Nasal Organoids.
-   Managed the lab GitHub repositories and computing resources.
-   Mentored students and research assistants on bioinformatics and data analysis.

### Sequencing and Bioinformatics Core Director / Assistant Investigator

The Forsyth Institute

Cambridge, MA

Nov/2017 - Aug/2019

-   Developed and validated a comprehensive workflow for analysis of 16S rRNA gene tag sequencing data that uses a training set derived from the Expanded Human Oral Microbiome Database (eHOMD) in conjunction with high-resolution algorithms, to allow species-level identification of oral, nasal and skin bacteria.
-   Supervised improvements on the 16S rRNA gene V1-V3 microbiome NGS library preparation to achieve longer and more informative reads that, combined with the use of eHOMD, allowed an even higher percentage of species-level assignment.
-   Managed the team of research associates and bioinformaticians on the day to day operations of the Core to serve internal and external clients (academic collaborations and commercial services).

### Research / Post-Doctoral Fellow (K.P. Lemon Lab)

The Forsyth Institute / Harvard School of Dental Medicine

Cambridge, MA

Nov/2012 - Nov/2017

-   Investigated small-molecule-mediated interactions between *Cutibacterium* spp. and *Staphylococcus aureus*, studying their impact on *S. aureus* biofilm formation and aggregation behavior.
-   Led the expansion of the Human Oral Microbiome Database (eHOMD) and its high-resolution RDP classifier training set to encompass bacteria from the entire human aerodigestive/respiratory tract.
